clue.text: Son wearing real bling — possibly sounds familiar!

indicators.note: the son is worn by the rearranged letters, so it goes inside them
possibly says the letters of the two words may be arranged some other way

explanation.surface: A young man decked in flashy jewellery strikes someone as vaguely recognisable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges REAL BLING into RING A BELL, and 'wearing' puts S (son) inside it, after RING.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: when something rings a bell it stirs a memory, so it seems familiar.

clue.text: Unlikely controller of viewing choices?

definitions.meaning: a ... chance is a slim, improbable one
the handset used to change television channels

explanation.surface: A device that is improbable as the thing that governs what we watch.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a slim chance is described as distant, and the TV handset is commonly called by the same short word.

clue.text: Exhibition centre tariff halved for drink

parts.note: NEC is the National Exhibition Centre in Birmingham, a big UK venue for trade shows

indicators.note: halved keeps just the front half of the six-letter word tariff

explanation.surface: A trade-show venue cuts its prices by half on beverages.
explanation.walkthrough: The NEC is the National Exhibition Centre, Birmingham's large events venue. 'halved' keeps the first three letters of TARIFF, giving TAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Nectar is the drink of the gods in myth, and loosely any delicious drink or fruit juice.

clue.text: Thoughtless broadcast knocked on the head

parts.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it widely
brained means struck hard on the head

explanation.surface: A careless remark is broadcast, and the speaker is metaphorically clobbered for it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' looks like radio or TV, but it is the old farming sense of strewing seed.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a scatterbrained person is forgetful and disorganised, acting without due thought.

clue.text: Born fool wrapping complete tree

indicators.note: the first pair of pieces wraps round the next one, which sits between them

parts.note: a nut is a crazy or foolish person
utter means complete, as in utter nonsense

explanation.surface: A natural idiot is described as wrapping up an entire tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrapping' has 'Born fool' read as one unit, the abbreviation and the synonym together, which then encloses the word for complete.
explanation.definitionFit: The butternut is a North American walnut tree, also called white walnut.

clue.text: Bug in plot must get discovered

indicators.note: dis-covered means with the covers taken off, so each of the three words loses its outer letters

explanation.surface: An insect in the garden bed is bound to be found eventually.
explanation.walkthrough: 'discovered' reads as 'found', but here it strips the first and last letter from PLOT, MUST and GET, leaving LO, US and E.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the louse is a small parasitic insect, and bug is a loose word for any insect.

clue.text: Worker not out to provide cover for injury?

definitions.meaning: a strikebreaker, a worker who refuses to go out on strike
the dry crust that forms over a healing wound

explanation.surface: A cricketer still batting arranges protection for a hurt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not out' suggests cricket, but here it means not on strike.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: a strikebreaker is called this insultingly, and the crust over a healing graze shares the name.

clue.text: Sort of bank making so much profit?

definitions.meaning: a high-street bank that settles cheques through the ... house system
to clear a sum is to make it as net profit

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about which kind of bank earns so much money.
explanation.walkthrough: A clearing bank is the British term for a major high-street bank.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: the type of bank that settles cheques, and netting a stated amount of profit.

clue.text: So a fish might be beaten

definitions.meaning: fish fried in a coating of flour and egg mixture, as in a chip shop
struck repeatedly, worn out by blows

explanation.surface: A fish might likewise end up thrashed.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish and chips in Britain usually means fish fried in a coating of batter.
explanation.definitionFit: Two senses: coated before frying, and pummelled by repeated blows.

clue.text: Cleaner that boosts operating team's morale?

definitions.meaning: an antiseptic alcohol used to clean skin
taken whimsically, the spirit or morale of a team in the operating theatre

explanation.surface: A product that cheers up the doctors and nurses in theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: The second half reads the name literally: surgical as in the operating team, spirit as in their morale.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgical spirit is the British name for methylated alcohol used to disinfect skin, known as rubbing alcohol elsewhere.

clue.text: Instant tea or coffee

parts.note: a mo is a moment or instant, as in wait a mo
cha (or char) is British slang for tea

explanation.surface: A choice at the café between quick tea or coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Instant' looks like instant coffee, but it is a moment, MO.
explanation.definitionFit: Mocha is a fine coffee originally shipped from the Yemeni port, now also a chocolate-flavoured coffee drink.

clue.text: Quarrelsome culture developing, not without love

indicators.note: developing says the letters change and grow into a new form
without says the letter for love is taken out of the word not

parts.note: love is zero in tennis scoring, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A combative culture takes shape, and it is not short of affection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes O (love) from NOT to leave NT, and 'developing' rearranges CULTURE with NT.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a truculent person is aggressively defiant and eager to argue.

clue.text: Row mainly about oven snack food

indicators.note: about means going round, so the shortened row surrounds the oven
mainly keeps most of the word, dropping its last letter

parts.note: a tier is a row of seats, one above another
an oast is a kiln for drying hops, as in an oast house in Kent

explanation.surface: An argument mostly concerns the oven and some snacks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Row' looks like a quarrel but is a tier; 'mainly' cuts it to TIE, and 'about' wraps that round OAST.
explanation.definitionFit: A toasted sandwich is called this in Britain, a common quick snack.

clue.text: What may be said in fencing part of kitchen garden?

definitions.text: What may be said in fencing

indicators.note: part of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A puzzle over what might be uttered behind the fence round a vegetable plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fencing' suggests garden fences, which the kitchen garden reinforces, but it is the sport.
explanation.definitionFit: The call a fencer gives to warn an opponent to take a guard position before a bout.

clue.text: Feminine anger about foul-smelling resin

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the first pair of pieces goes round the foul-smelling one

parts.note: to incense someone is to anger them
rank means smelling strongly and unpleasantly

explanation.surface: A woman is furious about a stinking gum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'concerning', but it makes 'Feminine anger' surround 'foul-smelling'.
explanation.definitionFit: An aromatic gum resin from Boswellia trees, burnt as an incense, one of the gifts of the Magi.

clue.text: Come up with gold on end of any list of stock

parts.note: to invent is to come up with a new idea
or is gold in heraldry

indicators.note: end of picks the final letter of the word any

explanation.surface: Devise a gold-based record of every item held.
explanation.walkthrough: OR is the heraldic word for gold.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an inventory is a complete itemised record of goods held.

clue.text: Provided a fine cross and Spain scored at last

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
to ford a river is to cross it
E is the international vehicle code for Spain (España)

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word scored

explanation.surface: A football match: a fine cross is delivered and Spain finally score.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cross' is a football pass here, but its letters come from crossing a river.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym in the sense of supplying: what you have afforded someone you have given them.

clue.text: Makes advances, ignoring the first two fearsome women

indicators.note: ignoring the first two drops the opening pair of letters from the synonym

parts.note: progresses means moves forward, makes headway

explanation.surface: Someone makes a pass at two frightening women, but skips the first pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Makes advances' sounds amorous, but it means moving forward.
explanation.definitionFit: Female monsters of folklore, and figuratively frightening, formidable women.

clue.text: Verify guilt, turning around answer, in a manner of speaking

indicators.note: around means the rearranged letters go round the single letter
turning signals the letters are turned about into a new order

explanation.surface: A detective confirms guilt, flipping a reply round, so to speak.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning' rearranges VERIFY GUILT, and 'around' puts A (answer) inside the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Speaking figuratively means not literally, which is what the phrase about a manner of speaking conveys.

clue.text: Stitch up trade union in firm

indicators.note: in places the trade union inside the word for firm

parts.note: sure means firm or secure, as in sure footing

explanation.surface: A union is framed by the company it works for.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stitch up' reads as framing someone, and 'firm' as a company; firm is SURE here.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgical stitch that closes a wound is called a suture.

clue.text: The man in optimum environment for command

indicators.note: in places the man inside the word for optimum
environment means surroundings, so the optimum word surrounds the man

parts.note: best means optimum, the top choice
he is the pronoun for the man

explanation.surface: A man in ideal surroundings gives the orders.
explanation.definitionFit: Done at someone's behest means done at their command or bidding.

clue.text: Nothing to write home? Good opportunity

parts.note: O looks like zero, nothing
to pen a letter is to write it
in means at home

explanation.surface: Having no news to send to the family is a good chance to rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nothing to write home about' is an idiom for something unremarkable, but it splits into pieces here.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: an opening is a chance, such as a job vacancy or a gap to exploit.

clue.text: Country found in rough anagram?

indicators.note: found in says the answer sits inside the words that follow, across their join

explanation.surface: A nation that turns up in a crudely jumbled puzzle word.
explanation.walkthrough: 'anagram' tempts you to rearrange, but nothing is shuffled: the letters run straight across the two words.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: Ghana is a nation in West Africa.

clue.text: Tempo regularly found in new melody — one by Holst

indicators.note: found in places the alternate letters between the two outer pieces

parts.note: a tune is a melody

indicators.note: regularly picks every other letter of the word tempo

explanation.surface: A steady beat runs through a fresh tune by the English composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'regularly' takes the even letters of the tempo word, and 'found in' sets them between the new and melody pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Holst's suite The Planets has seven movements, each named for a planet, including this one, the Mystic.

clue.text: Read about being imprisoned by tyrant with no time for criminal

indicators.note: imprisoned by says the rearranged letters go inside the shortened tyrant
with no says the letter for time is removed

parts.note: a despot is a tyrant

indicators.note: about here means turned around into a new order

explanation.surface: A book about someone jailed by a dictator who has no time for crooks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read' is fodder, not a verb: 'about' rearranges it, 'with no' strips time from the tyrant, and 'being imprisoned by' sets the jumble inside what is left.
explanation.definitionFit: A desperado is a reckless outlaw, especially of the Wild West, a type of criminal.

clue.text: Journey plan for English after overwhelming defeat

indicators.note: after places English following the defeat

parts.note: a rout is a crushing defeat

explanation.surface: A travel itinerary for the English team after a thrashing.
explanation.definitionFit: A route is the way planned for a journey from start to finish.

clue.text: Do be quiet — there's money

parts.note: sh is the sound telling someone to be quiet

explanation.surface: Please keep your voice down: there is cash about.
explanation.walkthrough: DO is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Dosh is British slang for cash.

clue.text: Simple area of postman's work offering financial security

parts.note: easy means simple
a postman delivers along a street, his round

explanation.surface: An undemanding postal round turns out to pay well.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom: living on easy street means being comfortably well off, free of money worries.
